verdict.rationale: Foreloop documents a bug-to-PR workflow. Its own agent reads a user-reported submission, fills in the intention and proposes tasks. A coding agent you run (Claude Code or Codex) then polls for approved tasks, claims one, does the work and opens a pull request. The diagnosis step is Foreloop's own, but the fix runs in a third-party agent on your own machine, and nothing runs until a person approves the contract, so it is not fully autonomous. missing for 10: Foreloop-native execution of the fix rather than reliance on an external agent, evidence of fix quality or success rates, independent or hands-on corroboration, autonomy without the human approval gate.

support.subject: As a developer, I can have an agent autonomously diagnose and fix a reported bug

citations.quote: An intention starts from the report, and its agent reads the submission, fills in the intention, and proposes the tasks
That agent asks Foreloop for approved tasks in that repository, claims one, does the work, and opens a pull request from your GitHub account.
The agent then checks Foreloop for approved tasks on a cadence and works them as they arrive.
Nothing runs until a person approves a contract.
